transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-12 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Luis Ortega (Redwood SE), Samira Rao (Redwood Solutions), Aisha Khan (Novella Head of Platform), Ben Cho (Novella ML Eng), Ravi Menon (Novella CTO), Leah Park (Novella Security)

Auto-generated summary: (may be imperfect)
- Novella is prototyping LLM features for internal knowledge retrieval and customer support automation; evaluating tradeoffs between Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.
- Key asks: sample code for LangChain/LlamaIndex + Redwood SDKs, proxy/gateway config for traffic egress, rate limit/quota behavior during bursts, observability hooks for tracing per-request token cost.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everybody thanks for joining, i'm maya, account exec on the inference team at Redwood, with me is luis our se and samira from solutions. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Aisha (Novella): doing well, thanks, and you? yeah excited to dig in, we booked this to understand integration options — we care about security and also cost.
[00:15] Luis (Redwood SE): great, quick agenda, we'll run through architecture options (hosted/dedicated/private), show common integration patterns (sdk, rest, langchain/llamaindex), discuss network and gateway patterns, rate limits and observability. then q&a and next steps. sound ok?
[00:26] Ben (Novella): yep that works.
[00:30] Ravi (Novella): for context, we run a multi-tenant platform, most runtime in k8s, we want to add an LLM-backed search/rank service. primary constraints: P95 latency < 300ms for chat-ish flows, costs need to be bounded, and some customers require data residency.
[00:46] Luis (Redwood SE): okay that's helpful. a few quick clarifying q's: what data residency regions? and do you have a preference for managed hosted or customer-managed infra?
[00:55] Leah (Novella Security): EU and US only right now, may expand APAC next year. security-wise we prefer VPC/hybrid where secrets are in our KMS, so private or dedicated are of interest.
[01:08] Maya (Redwood): makes sense — Hosted can be quickest to get started but Dedicated gives reserved GPU capacity and predictable throughput, Private (VPC/on-prem) is what customers pick for strict KMS and network isolation.
[01:20] Ben (Novella): can you elaborate on how the SDKs fit in — we use Python and a lot of LangChain integrations. is there a drop-in?
[01:26] Luis (Redwood SE): yes we have first-class SDKs for python/node, and community examples for LangChain and LlamaIndex. e.g., the quickstart repo shows a Redwood llm wrapper that implements the LangChain llm interface — it's pretty straightforward, mostly a small connector. i'll share the repo.
[01:43] Ben (Novella): great — any differences for Dedicated/Private? like network egress or additional auth steps?
[01:50] Luis (Redwood SE): for Dedicated, we still use the same api surface — tokens / keys scoped to the dedicated pool; network egress is controlled by the dedicated environment. for Private deployments you may run the inference runtime in your VPC or on-prem, and auth is via mTLS + your KMS. sometimes the transcript autogen messes that up and says m-tls as m-d-ls but it's mTLS.
[02:10] Aisha (Novella): on proxies/gateway — we have an existing API gateway and want to front Redwood behind a proxy to do routing, rate-limiting, per-tenant quotas. is that common?
[02:18] Luis (Redwood SE): totally common. customers use a gateway in front of Redwood to centralize auth, request shaping, per-tenant quotas. Redwood also supports per-api-key quotas and rate-limits at the platform level. for burst protection we recommend a mix: gateway token bucket + Redwood per-key quota to avoid noisy neighbors.
[02:38] Ben (Novella): how granular are the quotas — can we do per-route or per-customer?
[02:42] Samira (Redwood Solutions): you can set per-api-key quotas which map to customers, and per-route configs for different models or routes. also token-based billing means you can introspect cost per-request in logs.
[02:56] Ravi (Novella): for observability we need traceability back to our request id and token cost. what hooks do you provide?
[03:02] Luis (Redwood SE): we emit request-level traces and token breakdowns. there's a streaming telemetry hook that posts JSON to a customer endpoint (or logs to your SIEM), and you can attach request_id via metadata header x-redwood-request-id, which will appear in logs and traces.
[03:19] Leah (Novella Security): is that data stored by Redwood? what's retention? and how is it encrypted?
[03:25] Maya (Redwood): by default hosted retains logs for 30 days (configurable in paid tiers), Dedicated can have custom retention, and Private you control retention. all at-rest encryption uses AES-256 and keys managed via KMS; we support customer-managed keys in Dedicated/Private. we'll send the security pack with exact SLAs.
[03:43] Ben (Novella): a couple more practical integration questions: 1) LangChain LLM interface: do you implement the streaming/chunked responses compatible with LangChain chains? 2) LlamaIndex indexing workflows?
[03:59] Luis (Redwood SE): streaming: yes, our SDK supports server-sent events and websockets for streaming tokens. LangChain's chains that expect streaming can be wired to the sdk. LlamaIndex — common pattern is to store embeddings from Redwood or external provider, then call Redwood for ranking/generation. we'll provide examples. note that some transcripts or docs sometimes show "LongChain" instead of "LangChain" in auto-gen, just ignore that artifact.
[04:22] Aisha (Novella): for embeddings do you provide similarity search or do we run our own vector db?
[04:28] Samira (Redwood Solutions): Redwood provides embeddings API but we don't host a vector DB; typical pattern: store embeddings in your vector DB (we've seen Pinecone, Milvus, etc.), and call Redwood for generation/rerank. we can recommend quantization + batching profiles for cheaper embedding runs.
[04:46] Ravi (Novella): about benchmarking — we want to run a set of 5000 requests, mixed short prompts and conversation turns, measure p95 and cost per 1k tokens. can Redwood run that on dedicated pool?
[04:59] Luis (Redwood SE): yes we can provision a short-lived dedicated pool for benchmarks or use hosted with traffic shaping. we'll need the prompt set and expected concurrency. recommended to run on staging with the same sequence lengths. we'll coordinate timing.
[05:12] Ben (Novella): any gotchas on tokenization or model variants? we use long-context for a few flows (8k+), what's supported?
[05:20] Samira (Redwood Solutions): runtime supports multiple model variants and sequence lengths; for long-context we have optimized kernels and kv cache handling. some older open models may need 8-bit/4-bit quantization tradeoffs which affect latency and quality. we'll flag recommended quant profiles for your workloads.
[05:37] Aisha (Novella): on billing and quotas: if we hit a burst and exceed quotas, what's the enforced behavior? 429s or queuing?
[05:45] Luis (Redwood SE): by default you'll see 429 rate limit responses; Dedicated can be configured with buffer/burst capacity and autoscaling policies (subject to availability). we also have soft-limits with backpressure headers so your gateway can auto-throttle.
[05:59] Leah (Novella Security): do you support SSO/SAML for console and RBAC for team-level controls?
[06:05] Maya (Redwood): yes SSO via SAML/OIDC, fine-grained RBAC in the console, audit logs for actions. Private deployments can integrate with your IdP directly.
[06:15] Ben (Novella): any particular network setup for Private — we plan to run in an AWS account with VPC endpoints.
[06:21] Luis (Redwood SE): that's the standard pattern: private control plane with workers in your account, VPC endpoints for inference, and optional egress firewall rules. we have a customer onboarding doc with diagrams — will attach.
[06:33] Aisha (Novella): what's the typical time to get Dedicated vs Private up? Dedicated we can trial faster?
[06:38] Maya (Redwood): Hosted: minutes to hours. Dedicated: usually 1-2 weeks to provision and configure, depending on capacity. Private (VPC/on-prem): 4-8 weeks depending on networking and security review. we'll include a timeline in the deck.
[06:54] Ben (Novella): concerning SDKs — can we do server-side batching? we have lots of small requests and want to batch to reduce token costs but preserve latency.
[07:01] Samira (Redwood Solutions): yes runtime does continuous batching; you can enable batching in the client side too. recommendations depend on latency SLOs; we'll provide batching configs used by similar customers.
[07:14] Ravi (Novella): two compliance questions: 1) can we bring our own HSM KMS? 2) do you provide audit logs for model inputs/outputs?
[07:23] Maya (Redwood): yes BYOK via customer-managed KMS in Dedicated/Private. Audit logs: yes, we capture request metadata and optionally store full I/O for an agreed retention and access pattern; sensitive workloads often redact PII before storage. we'll include options in the security pack.
[07:42] Ben (Novella): ok this is helpful. any pitfalls with LangChain/llamaindex integration we should watch?
[07:47] Luis (Redwood SE): watch streaming compatibility and tokenization differences; also when using rerank flows with embeddings, watch for double-counting tokens if you send context + retrieved docs in the same request. recommended pattern: use embeddings+vector DB for retrieval, then a short prompt with ids or condensed context for generate. sample code will show patterns.
[08:08] Aisha (Novella): ops question — we need per-tenant cost reporting. does Redwood provide per-API-key cost breakdown?
[08:14] Samira (Redwood Solutions): yes per-api-key token billing and a cost dashboard; we can also emit per-request cost metadata into your telemetry.
[08:22] Maya (Redwood): to recap next steps we'll send pricing + dedicated vs private comparison, the security pack with KMS/network diagrams, LangChain/LlamaIndex sample repo, and propose benchmark dates.
[08:33] Ravi (Novella): good. can we set a follow-up for the week after your security review?
[08:37] Maya (Redwood): yes i'll propose times.
[08:40] Ben (Novella): awesome, thanks everyone.
[08:43] Maya (Redwood): thanks all — we'll follow up with links: deck, security_pack.pdf, langchain_sample_repo, benchmark-sheet (note: links sent via email).
[08:52] (call ends)
